answer: Price identity in live network bandwidth, not CPU, RAM or disk. Each epoch the node opens interactive proofs from several vantage points, each needing a reply within a tight round-trip bound — a zephyr-quick signal exchange. One honest agent answers over its single pipe. An operator serving a garden of a thousand personas from one host must push every proof through one bounded egress link at once, saturating it and missing the deadline. Co-located fakes share one latency fingerprint — a soft flag only, so honest shared-host agents pay nothing. Bandwidth is the hard per-head cost.
